barCharacter: Vera Oberlin. She is the cast's status apex, and her lines are transactional put-downs that treat the player as staff ('my most trusted advisor'). The corpus holds only 9 Vera lines plus 3 narrator lines about her (#53-55), so all 12 were used.

ours12: Escalate me, Miss Tilly. Do. There is nobody above me.
Thank you for offering, Mr Brock; the trunks are upstairs.
Put the fee on his room. Then remove the room.
Left, you say. Very well. The building will turn.
Mr Brock, my wig moved. My wig does not move.
We have had four princes this month. Two paid.
I have expensive taste. I once sent back a sunset. How do you keep up?
Crumb. Persian carpet. You are shedding on a country.
Storm off again. Use the east doors. They slam better.
Madam, I recommend the door; people like you also chose it.
Your Highness, URGENT is not a volume we offer.
Sir Quill, your bill is in verse, and the final line is the door.
bar12: Sorry, I'm focusing on my career... my career on not dating losers like you! (#12)
Ugh, it's such a chore being this beautiful all the time. How am I ever going to get rid of him? (#45)
You'd be willing to cover up the literal murder I've committed, no questions asked. Right? (#47)
only [drinks] four things: scotch, red wine, the tears of [her] enemies, and straight up poison (#52)
Girl, we need to have a little talk about feminism. You, back me up on this. Tell her she doesn't need to poison herself for the sake of a man. (#51)
Now I just need to find a way to reinforce the superiority of the Cools over the Un-Cools. (#46)
I need a way to get ahead of the pack. And since you're SUCH a good advisor... (#49)
Come on, think of something! You're my most trusted advisor! (#50)
Narrator: Whoa. You know this is a serious situation if it's causing Vera to show empathy. (#55)
Narrator: You see Vera at the mirror, attempting to tame her hair with a cattle prod. (#54)
Narrator: You turn around to find Vera staring at you. This often happens, but for some reason it's not a death stare this time. (#53)
headToHead.voiceNote: Ours wins on voice. With the names covered, Maximilian's top twelve are all one man: a service courtesy ('Thank you for offering', 'Do', 'Very well') and then a ruling. Vera's corpus is thinner on shape: #50 and #49 could be any bossy cast member, and she is only unmistakable in #12, #45 and #47.
headToHead.constructionNote: Tie. Both sets are economical and put the turn on the last words ('Then remove the room', 'Two paid', 'Right?'). Vera has two devices ours lacks: the repeated-word fake-out (#12) and the complaint dressed as a boast (#45). Ours relies heavily on the suitor's gimmick for its turn (URGENT, recalculating, people like you also chose, escalate), which is legitimate rival use but means five of the twelve need the suitor's line to work.
headToHead.quotableNote: The bar wins. Vera clips because her presumptions are monstrous: she assumes you will cover up a murder, and she drinks poison and tears. Maximilian's presumptions top out at a tip, a robe, a minibar or a trunk. 'Put the fee on his room. Then remove the room.' and 'I once sent back a sunset' would get clipped. Most of the rest are tidy and petty, and petty does not travel out of context.

templates: Billing/tipping turn (36 lines): the blade lands on a bill, tip, rate, deposit, invoice or charge. Examples: 'I charge per attempt', 'I am billing three', 'I have tipped for less', 'I am the bill'. This is the bank's default ending.
Staff as the punchline (14): a porter, doorman, housekeeping, night porter, accountant or maitre d' delivers the joke. The persona bans exactly this.
Furniture or object as the victim (10): chandelier, carpet, marble, trouser press, lapels, ceiling, revolving door, furniture, and the soup three times. The persona also bans this.
Presumption plus a tag ('yes?', 'of course', 'naturally', 'as discussed', 'you agreed earlier'): 8 lines. It is the persona's engine, but the tag is now a reflex.
'How brave, [address], ...': 4 lines, counting the tipping one.
holdCard 'you both did X; only one of you stays/I keep one': 6 lines.
cardHint '{name}, you [past-tense verb]..., and I/which [consequence]': about 18 of 24 lines share this skeleton.
ruleBreaks: Word limits: none over. Every line is within its category limit (intro 14, questions 18, react/cardReact 10, cut 14, twistIntro 18, oneOnOne 14, hold 12, pick 16, outro 12, bottom 12, cutFrames 14, cardHint 14, verdict 12, compare 12, holdCard 14, pickFrames 16).
Em dashes, emoji, exclamation marks, contractions, 'as an AI', therapy talk, stock romance filler, real people or brands: none found.

The persona bans leaning on owning things, but these do: 'Mr Dash, you are blacklisted from every hotel I own. Which is most hotels.' / 'Nav, direct me to the best room in my own hotel, without looking.' / 'Kindly do not read my own menu back to me.'

The persona says 'one unbroken courteous sentence; fragments only for a one-word ruling', but these are chains of fragments: 'Sir Quill. The key. You will call it something ridiculous. Allowed.' / 'Crumb. The suite. You are on the nightstand. Do not pop before seven.' / 'Your Highness, dinner is on you. You offered. In the email. Yes?' / 'Darling. Cancel my nine o'clock. And the decade.' / 'Policy, recited. How very night shift.' / 'Your Highness, the shorts stay. The crown stays. The flip-flops have been destroyed.' (also a tricolon list)
List: 'Our future, three words exactly. You may borrow mine. Suite. Silence. Me.' The twist asks for three words, so this is a mild case.
The persona says no pet names, and this uses one: 'Good boy, Mr Brock. I mean that as a promotion.'

These charmed reactions read as cold, so the visible mark misleads bettors (FORMAT2 fault 2): 'Nav, you have been given the space nearest the door.' / 'Kind, Miss Tilly; I shall find out who paid you.' / 'Miss Tilly, your shift starts at six; nobody told you?'

Cuts that are too soft for a star, gentle send-offs with no blade: 'Mr Brock, leave at any speed you like; I shall be timing it.' / 'Nav, you will find the exit faster than I can point; begin.' / 'Your carriage awaits, Sir Quill. I had it built in your century.'
Contradicts the persona's ego (elsewhere he calls magnificence 'accurate'): '{name}, nobody is that impressed by me, so I asked myself why.'
biggestGap: His presumption never escalates past petty cash: in roughly a third of the bank the blade lands on a tip, bill, rate or member of staff. Vera, by contrast, presumes you will cover up a murder. In the next pass, cap money, tip and staff endings at one per section. Rewrite the rest so that Maximilian calmly assumes the suitor is already complicit in something outrageous and specific that only a five-star concierge would arrange (a body in the laundry, a duke's forged signature, an evacuated wing), and keep the courtesy exactly as polite.
